title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Postmortems, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Comms Templates
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard incident lifecycle, on-call rotations and handoffs, runbook templates for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, game-day exercises, and canonical status page / customer communications templates. It is intended as the single source of truth for incident management across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment products.

Scope:
- Applies to all production incidents that affect customer-facing availability, latency, data integrity, or security across Redwood-hosted and customer-managed runtimes where Redwood has operational responsibility.
- Excludes purely internal CI failures or developer workstation issues unless they affect production SLOs.

Definitions and Roles:
- Incident Commander (IC): Leads the response, makes prioritization and mitigation decisions, owns incident timeline and postmortem coordination.
- Primary Responder: The first engineer paged for the service (Pod/service owner).
- Secondary/Backup: Cross-team backup for escalation when primary cannot resolve.
- Scribe/Communications Lead: Captures timeline, actions, and writes status updates.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Domain owners for networking, storage, model-serving runtime, infra, and security.
- PagerDuty: Source of truth for on-call escalation and contactability.

SLOs & Alerting Thresholds (Examples):
- Generation API availability: 99.95% monthly uptime target.
- Error rate (4xx+5xx) threshold for P1 page: >0.5% of requests for 5m sustained or >0.2% at 95th token cost impact.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency > 1.5s for >10m sustained or >2x baseline for a service = P1/P2 depending on customer impact.
- Queue backlog / capacity exhaustion: queue length > 5k requests or GPU utilization > 95% for 10m = P1.

Incident Severity Matrix (triage guidance):
1) P0 (SEV1) — Total outage or data-loss: customer-facing downtime impacting >30% customers or active data loss. Pager: All-hands; IC assigned immediately.
2) P1 (SEV2) — Major degradation: significant latency or error-rate increase impacting production SLAs. Pager: Primary + IC.
3) P2 (SEV3) — Partial degradation / feature impairment. Pager: Primary or async slack.
4) P3 (SEV4) — Minor issues, usability, or internal errors not impacting customer SLAs.

Incident Lifecycle (High level):
1) Detect & Page
   - Alerts fire into PagerDuty. On-call primary is paged. If no acknowledgement in 5 minutes escalate to backup.
2) Triage (First 10 minutes)
   - Primary responder assesses: Is this a P0/P1/P2? If P0/P1, assign IC and Scribe.
   - Post a short summary in the incident channel (#incident-<id>) and update the status page to "investigating".
3) Respond & Mitigate (10-60 minutes)
   - IC coordinates containment actions (traffic reroute, rollback, scale-up, circuit breakers).
   - Apply runbook steps for the affected service (see Runbook Templates).
4) Restore & Verify (60+ minutes as needed)
   - Confirm service health via dashboards and synthetic tests. Gradually remove mitigations when safe.
5) Communicate
   - Provide status updates at a regular cadence (initial within 30 minutes, then every 60 minutes for P1/P0 until recovery).
   - Notify Customer Success for any customer-facing comms/action.
6) Post-incident
   - Launch a blameless postmortem within 72 hours for P0/P1; draft due in 7 days with action owners and target dates.

Runbook Templates (canonical, apply verbatim where applicable):
- Runbook: API generation high error rate
  Description: Spike in 5xx or model failures for generation endpoints.
  Detection: Alerts: /metrics/api_errors 5xx_rate > 0.5% 5m; Synthetics failing.
  Immediate actions (IC / Primary Responder):
    1) Collect context: service name, deployment ID, recent deploys (kubectl get deploy -o wide), commit sha.
    2) Check control plane & infra: cloud console health, cluster node count, autoscaler events.
    3) Run quick health checks:
       - curl -sS https://console.redwood.internal/health/<service>
       - kubectl logs -n production <pod> --since=5m | tail -n 200
    4) If errors indicate model load or OOMs: scale pod count or move traffic to a healthy variant (retire bad instances).
    5) If recent deploy suspected: rollback to previous stable deploy: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> -n production
    6) If GPU exhaustion: scale Dedicated pools or offload low-priority traffic.
  Verification: Run synthetic generation tests (100 requests at target distribution) and confirm 95th latency and error rate within SLO.
  Escalation: If unresolved after 20 minutes, page Model Runtime SME and infra SRE.

- Runbook: High latency for generation endpoint
  Steps:
    1) Identify latency characteristics: tail vs. median, affected models, sequence lengths.
    2) Check KV cache hit rates and batching queues.
    3) If batching backlog is high: temporarily reduce batch size or increase worker count. CLI examples:
       - redis-cli HGET all prefix_cache_hit_rate
       - kubectl exec -it <pod> -c runtime -- /bin/sh -c "ps aux | grep runtime"
    4) If kernel-level stalls suspected, pull latest profiler snapshot and involve runtime team.

- Runbook: Capacity exhaustion (GPU / quota)
  Steps:
    1) Verify utilization: cloud provider console + internal capacity dashboard.
    2) Trigger emergency autoscale policy (see dashboard control: /ops/autoscale/policies).
    3) Apply throttling policy for best-effort customers, ensure Enterprise/Dedicated SLAs preserved via routing policies.
    4) Communicate to customers via status page and targeted emails if degradation persists > 30 minutes.

Service Ownership & Runbook Mapping (examples):
- service: api-gateway — owner: eng-platform — runbook: docs/runbooks/api-gateway.md
- service: runtime-inference — owner: eng-serving-runtime — runbook: docs/runbooks/runtime-inference.md
- service: model-catalog — owner: applied-ml-and-evals — runbook: docs/runbooks/model-catalog.md
(Owners and runbook links maintained in the Runbook Index; update immediately on team changes.)

Postmortem Template (required fields for P0/P1):
- Title (short):
- Incident ID / PagerDuty link:
- Date/time window (start — end):
- Summary (TL;DR, ~2 sentences):
- Impact (customers, internal, revenue SLOs):
- Timeline (chronological bullets with timestamps):
- Root cause (concise):
- Contributing factors (list):
- Corrective actions taken during incident (short list):
- Long-term mitigations & action items (owner, due date, status):
- Lessons learned & follow-ups (including doc updates, tests, runbook changes):
- Postmortem author & reviewers: 

Postmortem process and SLAs:
- Owner (IC) must assign a postmortem author within 24 hours.
- Draft due within 7 calendar days.
- Action items must have owners and a target date; owners must update status weekly until closed.
- For high-impact incidents, schedule a cross-team review during the next weekly incident retro.

On-call Rotations & Handoffs:
- Rotation cadence: primary on-call rotates weekly (Mon 09:00 to next Mon 09:00 local). Secondary backup rotates monthly.
- Shift length rationale: weekly rotations provide continuity and minimize fatigue while supporting predictable coverage for distributed teams.
- Handoffs: outgoing engineer must produce a 15 minute overlap summary with active incidents, outstanding tickets, and any scheduled maintenance. Use the On-call Handoff template in Slack and mark availability in PagerDuty calendar.
- Escalation policy: 5 minutes to acknowledge, 15 minutes to start triage. If unresolved after 30 minutes escalate to IC.

Game Days (recommended annual schedule & checklist):
- Frequency: at least quarterly per major product area (API, runtime, dedicated, private).
- Example scenarios: large traffic surge, region failure, model-serving kernel regression, private deployment offline, key compromise (tabletop only).
- Game Day checklist:
  1) Define objectives and success criteria (availability targets, recovery time).
  2) Run the scenario with live tooling; capture timings and bottlenecks.
  3) Validate runbook applicability and update docs.
  4) Produce a short report with action items and assign owners.

Status Page & Customer Communications (templates and cadence):
- Status levels: investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved.
- Recommended cadence for P1/P0: initial status within 30 minutes, subsequent updates every 60 minutes until monitoring, final post-incident summary within 48 hours.

Template: Initial status (status.redwood.example - paste to status page):
  Title: Investigating — Elevated errors on Generation API
  Impact: Customers may experience increased 5xx errors or failed generation requests for some models.
  Latest update: We have identified elevated error rates impacting a subset of generation requests. Engineers are investigating.
  Next update: In 30 minutes or sooner.

Template: Customer-facing update (email/snippet):
  Subject: Incident update — Generation API errors (start: 2026-02-15 14:12 UTC)
  Body:
  Hello —

  We are investigating increased error rates affecting generation requests in our Hosted region. Our engineers have identified the affected services and are actively working on mitigation. We will provide the next update within 30 minutes. We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a root cause summary.

  If you have urgent concerns or a dedicated account, please reply to this message or contact your Customer Success representative.

Template: Final post-incident summary (status page & customer email):
  Title: Resolved — Generation API error spike (root cause & mitigations)
  Summary: The issue was caused by a malformed model artifact deployed in the runtime cluster, which caused model initialization failures and elevated 5xx error rates.
  Impact: Approximately 12% of generation requests to the Hosted region failed between 14:12 and 15:05 UTC.
  Root cause: Bad artifact in deployment pipeline (regression introduced by commit sha abc123).
  Mitigation: Immediate rollback to previous artifact and validation added to deployment pipeline.
  Long-term actions: Add artifact validation step, improve canary traffic split for model deploys, add additional synthetic checks for model init latency. Action items assigned to owners with due dates.

Communication best practices:
- Keep messages short and factual. Avoid speculative root-cause statements until confirmed.
- Coordinate external comms with Customer Success and Sales for enterprise customers.
- Use the incident channel for internal comms; use dedicated threads for customer communications drafts.

Operational tooling & dashboards (links are internal):
- Incident dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/incidents
- On-call calendar & PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/teams/redwood
- Capacity & autoscale dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/capacity
- Synthetic tests & probing: https://console.redwood.internal/synthetics

Runbook & Playbook Maintenance:
- Runbooks owned by service teams; owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any incident where the runbook was applied.
- Changes to runbooks must be reviewed by at least one cross-functional SME and recorded in the Runbook Index (update date required).

Appendices:
- On-call Handoff template (use in Slack / PagerDuty):
  - Current incidents: <list with ids>
  - Outstanding action items: <owner — item — due>
  - Known issues and mitigation state:
  - PagerDuty availability: <on-call until date/time>

- Quick CLI cheatsheet (examples):
  - kubectl get pods -n production -l app=<service> -o wide
  - kubectl logs -n production <pod> --since=10m | tee /tmp/logs.txt
  - curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/health

- Contact list (maintain in Vault):
  - eng-platform on-call: eng-platform@pagerduty.redwood.example
  - eng-serving-runtime SME: runtime-leads@redwood.example
  - Customer Success: cs-team@redwood.example

Document ownership and updates:
- Document owner: eng-sre (operational owner) — maintainers in eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime.
- Review cadence: Quarterly for process sections; immediate update after any P1/P0 incident.

If you find missing runbook steps, broken links, or outdated owner information, please file a doc update PR to the Runbook Index and notify the eng-sre owners.
